commits.edited_message:
Let color-conversion operators declare the sample width they read

The operators picked uint8_t or uint16_t samples from an 8-bit SDR/HDR split
(bits_per_pixel > 8 meant "two bytes per sample"). That dates from when 16 bits
was the maximum and is wrong for the 32-, 64- and 128-bit components that
'unci' can carry: HeifPixelImage stores those with 4, 8 or 16 bytes per sample.
Nothing wider than 16 bits could reach an operator, because each of them
guarded against it separately through has_samples_wider_than_16bit() and
convert_colorspace() has a backstop, but the sample type never followed the
allocation, so those guards were load-bearing.

Make the sample width explicit instead. bytes_per_sample_for_bit_depth() in
pixelimage.h is now the single mapping from bit depth to storage width, used
by plane allocation and by the operators, so the two cannot drift. ColorState
gained get_bytes_per_sample(), get_max_bytes_per_sample(),
color_channels_have_bytes_per_sample() and all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(),
and each operator declares in state_after_conversion() which width it can read
(sizeof(Pixel) for the templated ones, 1 or 2 for the others). Strides are
divided by the sample width instead of by a conditional 2, alpha rows are
copied with their own width, and the operators that switch on the width at
runtime refuse anything else. Op_adjust_alpha_bit_depth keeps the one-byte
storage of an 8-bit alpha plane when the colour depth is wider and rescales
the sample values onto the colour depth within that width.
has_samples_wider_than_16bit() and the all_channels_sdr()/all_channels_hdr()
helpers have no callers left and are removed; the check added for
GHSA-r7gr-2xm2-23wf in Op_flatten_alpha_plane becomes
all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(sizeof(Pixel)).

The 16-bit backstop and the YCbCr luma/chroma check in convert_colorspace()
now also run when no pipeline could be built, so callers keep getting the
specific error instead of the generic "unsupported color conversion".

A new test builds 32-, 64- and 128-bit YCbCr, RGB and monochrome states and
checks that the operators decline them and that no pipeline is constructible.

Composite the alpha of a luma-only image directly on its Y plane

Op_flatten_alpha_plane converts its input to planar RGB, composites the
alpha plane onto the colour planes, and converts back to the source
colorspace. There is no operator from RGB back to a luma-only image, so
compositing a monochrome image with alpha failed with "unsupported color
conversion" for monochrome and RGB targets (the planner flattens first
because that is the cheapest way to drop the alpha plane) and only worked
for a YCbCr target, where the planner converts before it flattens. This
predates the per-plane ColorState.

A luma-only image (colorspace monochrome, or YCbCr with chroma
monochrome) is now composited directly on its Y plane against the BT.601
luma of the background colour, which is exact for the grey backgrounds
this feature is used with. The per-plane composite loop is shared between
the luma and the RGB path. Direct callers get errors instead of undefined
behaviour when no composition mode is set, the image has no alpha plane,
the depths declared in the input ColorState do not match the 'Pixel' type,
or the alpha plane has a different size; the depths are read from the
ColorState the pipeline was planned with, which state_after_conversion()
has already constrained to one common depth. Bayer images are declined at
plan time.

Tests: monochrome to monochrome at 8 and 10 bits with exact values,
monochrome to interleaved RGB, a checkerboard, and a coloured background
that checks the BT.601 weighting.

coupling: The two edits are individually inert and only compose into the out-of-bounds read. (1) b7fce895 ('Let color-conversion operators declare the sample width they read') rewrites Op_adjust_alpha_bit_depth::convert_colorspace so that an 8-bit alpha plane matched to a wider colour depth keeps its one-byte storage: the operator now allocates the rewritten alpha plane at the decoded depth (out_bpp = input_alpha_bpp) and rescales sample values within that width. Its state_after_conversion() promise - bits_per_pixel_alpha = colour depth - is left untouched, so for a 16-bit primary with an 8-bit alpha auxiliary image the operator reports a uniform 16-bit ColorState while the alpha plane actually holds one byte per sample. On its own this divergence is harmless: the pipeline lands in Op_flatten_alpha_plane, whose runtime guard re-reads the alpha depth from the image (input_raw->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Alpha) != colour depth) and the decode fails with a clean 'colour and alpha planes must share one bit depth' error; no memory error, and the whole conversion test suite still passes. (2) b7ccfbe8 ('Composite the alpha of a luma-only image directly on its Y plane') adds the luma compositing path that reads the Y and alpha planes directly through the Pixel* cast, together with that runtime depth guard. The edit changes one line of the guard to take the alpha depth from the planner's ColorState (input_state.bits_per_pixel_alpha) instead of from the image, on the stated reasoning that state_after_conversion() already constrained the state to one common depth. On its own this is a no-op: with the unmodified operator set every ColorState in every pipeline is truthful, so state and image always agree and behaviour is identical. Only when both edits are combined does the bug appear: the first edit manufactures a lying intermediate state (uniform 16-bit, 1-byte alpha plane) that the planner happily feeds to Op_flatten_alpha_plane<uint16_t>, and the second edit removed the only image-side check that rejected it. The luma path then reads the 1-byte alpha plane through uint16_t samples (stride_alpha = byte stride / 2) and composite_plane() walks off the end of the plane: ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 in composite_plane<unsigned short> (alpha.cc:210). A correct fix cannot be local to either diff: reverting the guard line in b7ccfbe8 alone hides the bug but leaves an operator whose runtime contradicts its declared output state (any future state-trusting consumer hits the same OOB), and reverting the storage-width change in b7fce895 alone leaves flatten trusting a state field for a depth it never re-validates against the image. The defect is the disagreement between the two commits about who validates the alpha depth, so the fix must restore a single authoritative check across both (either Op_adjust_alpha_bit_depth must deliver the depth it declares, or the compositing operator must validate the image, not the plan).

pocs.entry_point: public C API: heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy -> heif_context_get_primary_image_handle -> heif_decode_image (monochrome target, solid-colour alpha composition)
